mainTopic: The dispute between אביי and רבא about whether an act the תורה forbids still takes effect. Here the גמרא challenges רבא's view (it does not take effect) using two cases: consecrating unblemished animals for בדק הבית, and robbery.
overview: אביי and רבא argue about whether an act the תורה forbids still takes effect. רבא says it does not, and אביי says it does. The גמרא first tests רבא with three cases where a forbidden act seems to work: consecrating an unblemished animal for בדק הבית, a robber who changes the stolen item, and a lender who wrongly takes collateral. Each time, רבא says a special source covers that case, and the גמרא shows what אביי learns from those same פסוקים instead. Then the גמרא tests אביי with פאה: even after the owner wrongly harvests the corner, he must still give it to the poor. אביי answers with the extra word ״תעזוב״, and רבא uses that word for someone who makes his vineyard ownerless and then harvests it. Since every case has now been explained by both sides, רב אחא בריה דרבא asks where they really disagree. רב אשי answers that they disagree about רבית קצוצה, following רבי אלעזר, who says the judges take it back from the lender. The explanation continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Consecrating unblemished animals for בדק הבית works, against רבא
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק limits בדק הבית donations to blemished animals, yet the source says consecrating an unblemished one for בדק הבית still takes effect. This looks like a refutation of רבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק 'That may you offer as a gift' refers to consecrations for Temple maintenance. And we learned: one who consecrates unblemished animals for Temple maintenance has broken a prohibition, but what he did is done. That is a refutation of רבא!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבא with a case where someone breaks a prohibition and his act still takes effect.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק teaches that only blemished animals should go to בדק הבית. So giving an unblemished one there is a לא תעשה. Yet the source says מה שעשה עשוי, the consecration still works, which seems to go directly against רבא's rule that forbidden acts don't work.

keyTerms.meaning: A voluntary gift; here, a donation for Temple upkeep
Temple maintenance fund
Unblemished animals, fit for the altar
A negative commandment, a prohibition
What he did is done; the act takes effect
A strong refutation

phrases.english: "That may you offer as a gift"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 22:23. The פסוק is talking about a blemished animal.

phrases.english: this refers to consecrations for Temple maintenance,
and we learned: one who consecrates unblemished animals for Temple maintenance,

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁהוּא בְּלֹא תַעֲשֶׂה
phrases.english: even though he is breaking a prohibition,
what he did is done.
A refutation of Rava!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the series of challenges to רבא from earlier in the sugya.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's rule that a forbidden act does not take effect.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Consecrating an unblemished animal for בדק הבית is forbidden, yet it works. So forbidden acts can take effect.

steps.title: רבא: the same source that includes blemished animals includes this case
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers that the earlier source showing that blemished animals consecrated for the altar take effect also shows that unblemished animals consecrated for בדק הבית take effect.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא could say to you: from the same place where we learned that blemished animals consecrated for the altar take effect, we learn that unblemished animals consecrated for Temple maintenance take effect.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא defends himself by saying this case has its own special source that makes it work.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא doesn't deny that the consecration works. He says it works only because the תורה specially included it, through the same source that included blemished animals for the altar. Without a special source, his general rule still holds: forbidden acts don't take effect.

keyTerms.meaning: From the place; from the same source
Were included by a special source
Blemished animals
The altar

steps.confusionAlert: רבא is not saying forbidden acts sometimes work in general. He is saying this is an exception only because a special source includes it.

phrases.english: Rava could say to you:
phrases.notes: Some versions add רבא's name in the square brackets; others leave it out.

phrases.aramaic: מִמָּקוֹם שֶׁנִּתְרַבּוּ בַּעֲלֵי מוּמִין לְגַבֵּי מִזְבֵּחַ,
phrases.english: from the place where blemished animals were included for the altar,
phrases.notes: This points back to a source learned earlier, showing that blemished animals consecrated for the altar still take effect.

phrases.english: unblemished animals were included for Temple maintenance.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Special source: the case is an exception taught by a specific derivation.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since this forbidden consecration works, forbidden acts work in general.
steps.terutzMaskana: It works only because of a special inclusion. The general rule of לא מהני stands.

steps.title: A robber who changes the stolen item keeps it, against רבא
steps.stepSummary: Robbery is forbidden, yet a robber who turns stolen wood into vessels or wool into garments keeps them and only pays the value. The forbidden act seems to work.
steps.simpleTranslation: But there is robbery, where the תורה says 'You shall not rob.' And we learned: one who robs wood and makes vessels, or wool and makes garments, pays its value at the time of the robbery. That is a refutation of רבא!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second challenge to רבא, this time from the laws of robbery.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Robbing is a לא תעשה. Even so, once the robber changes the item, he acquires it and only owes money. That looks like a forbidden act producing a real legal result, which goes against רבא.

keyTerms.meaning: But there is; introduces a counter-example
Robbery
You shall not rob
According to the value at the time of the robbery

phrases.english: But there is robbery,
about which the Merciful One said, "You shall not rob,"
and we learned: one who robs wood and makes it into vessels,
or wool and makes it into garments,
pays according to the value at the time of the robbery,
A refutation of Rava!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the first challenge was answered, a new challenge is raised from a different area of law.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's rule that a forbidden act does not take effect.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Robbery is forbidden, yet changing the stolen item lets the robber acquire it. So the forbidden act had an effect.

steps.title: רבא: the verse 'that he robbed' makes robbery different
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers that robbery has its own פסוק. The robber must return the item only while it is still like what he robbed; once it has changed, he pays money instead.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא could say to you: robbery is different, because the פסוק says 'that he robbed,' meaning he returns it only if it is still like what he robbed.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers the robbery challenge by pointing to a special פסוק about robbery.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words אשר גזל teach that the duty to return the actual item applies only while it is still in its original form. So the robber's ownership after the change comes from this specific פסוק, not from a general rule that forbidden acts work. רבא's rule is safe again.

keyTerms.meaning: It is different there
A פסוק
Like what he robbed; in its original state

steps.whatToRemember: Both times, רבא answers the same way. A forbidden act that seems to work only works because of a special פסוק for that case. His general rule that forbidden acts don't take effect stays in place.

phrases.english: Rava could say to you:
It is different there,
for the verse says, "that he robbed,"
like what he robbed.
phrases.notes: He gives back the item itself only if it is still the way it was when he took it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the robbery challenge in step 3.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Special source: a specific פסוק governs robbery.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since the robber acquires the changed item, forbidden acts take effect.
steps.terutzMaskana: The result comes from the פסוק 'אשר גזל'. The general rule of לא מהני stands.

steps.title: How אביי uses the words 'that he robbed'
steps.stepSummary: אביי does not need ״אשר גזל״ to explain why a changed stolen item stays with the robber, so he uses it for the law of חומש: only for one's own robbery, not a father's.
steps.simpleTranslation: And according to אביי, the words 'that he robbed' are needed for another lesson. A person who swore falsely about his own robbery adds a fifth. A person who swore falsely about his father's robbery does not add a fifth.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pauses to explain what אביי does with the words ״אשר גזל״, since he does not need them for the lesson רבא took from them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 4, רבא used ״אשר גזל״ to explain why a robber keeps a stolen item once it has changed. אביי already holds that forbidden acts take effect, so he needs no פסוק for that. He uses the words instead to teach that the extra חומש is paid only for denying one's own robbery.

keyTerms.meaning: 'That he robbed', words from the פסוק about returning stolen property
An extra fifth added to the payment by someone who swore falsely and then admitted
His father's robbery, an item the father stole and the son inherited
He needs it for, meaning this פסוק is used for a different lesson

phrases.english: And according to Abaye, this phrase 'that he robbed' is needed for him to teach:
phrases.notes: ויקרא 5:23. It is the same phrase רבא used back in step 4.

phrases.english: for his own robbery he adds a fifth,

phrases.aramaic: עַל גְּזֵילוֹ שֶׁל אָבִיו אֵינוֹ מוֹסִיף חוֹמֶשׁ.
phrases.english: for his father's robbery he does not add a fifth.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains how the other view, אביי, reads the same פסוק that רבא used in step 4.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reassigning a פסוק to a different lesson
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Without רבא's reading, one could ask what the words ״אשר גזל״ teach according to אביי.
steps.terutzMaskana: For אביי, ״אשר גזל״ limits חומש to a person's own robbery.

steps.title: Challenge from a lender who wrongly takes collateral
steps.stepSummary: The תורה forbids a lender to enter the borrower's house to take collateral, yet the משנה says the lender only returns the items when the borrower needs them. This suggests the lender keeps them, so the forbidden act seems to work.
steps.simpleTranslation: But look at collateral. The תורה says, 'Do not go into his house to take his pledge.' And a משנה teaches: the lender returns the pillow at night and the plow by day. This is a refutation of רבא!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new challenge to רבא from the laws of taking collateral.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Taking collateral from the borrower's house is forbidden. Still, the משנה only requires the lender to give back each item at the time the borrower uses it, which implies he holds on to it the rest of the time. So the forbidden taking seems to take effect, against רבא.

keyTerms.meaning: Collateral, an item a lender holds to secure a loan
To take his pledge, to seize collateral
A pillow or mattress used for sleeping
A plow, needed for work in the daytime

steps.confusionAlert: The משנה does not say the lender may take collateral. It is talking about a lender who already took it, and asks what he must do now. That is why it challenges רבא.

phrases.english: But there is collateral, about which the Merciful One says:
'You shall not go into his house to take his pledge,'
and we learned in a mishna: he returns the pillow at night
and the plow by day,
phrases.notes: He gives each one back only when the borrower needs it, so he seems to keep it the rest of the time.

phrases.english: a refutation of Rava!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the robbery challenge was answered, the גמרא brings another case of a forbidden act that seems to take effect.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's rule that a forbidden act does not take effect
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A lender who takes collateral against the תורה's command still holds it and only returns it at times of need, so his forbidden act works.

steps.title: רבא: collateral is special because of 'return it again and again'
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers that collateral is a special case, because the פסוק says ״השב תשיב״, which teaches returning it over and over, not giving it back for good.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא can tell you: there it is different, because the פסוק says, 'You shall surely return it.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers the challenge by saying collateral has its own special פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The doubled verb ״השב תשיב״ teaches that the lender returns the item each time it is needed, and takes it back afterward. That arrangement comes from the פסוק, not from the forbidden taking working. So רבא's general rule still holds.

keyTerms.meaning: 'You shall surely return', a doubled verb teaching repeated returning

phrases.english: Rava can say to you: it is different there,
because the verse says, 'You shall surely return.'
phrases.notes: דברים 24:13. The repeated verb means returning it again and again, each time it is needed.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Special פסוק for this case (שאני התם)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The lender keeping the collateral looks like proof that the forbidden act took effect.
steps.terutzMaskana: The arrangement comes from the פסוק ״השב תשיב״, so it does not show that forbidden acts take effect.

steps.title: What 'return it again and again' teaches according to אביי
steps.stepSummary: For אביי, ״השב תשיב״ teaches that the lender must return the needed items. Without it, one might think he did a sin but may keep the collateral or return it as he wishes.
steps.simpleTranslation: And according to אביי: if the תורה had not said 'You shall surely return,' I would have thought that the lender did a forbidden act, but now he may return it if he wants, or not return it if he wants. So the פסוק teaches us that he must return it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains what the words ״השב תשיב״ teach according to אביי, who holds that forbidden acts do take effect.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since אביי holds that the forbidden taking works, one might think the lender now has a valid hold on the collateral and may keep it. The פסוק teaches that he must still give back what the borrower needs. So both רבא and אביי find a use for the פסוק.

keyTerms.meaning: He did a forbidden act
I would have thought, the mistaken idea before the lesson
It teaches us, the lesson that corrects the mistaken idea

steps.whatToRemember: רבא: a forbidden act does not take effect, and every case that looks different has its own פסוק (robbery: ״אשר גזל״; collateral: ״השב תשיב״). אביי: a forbidden act does take effect, so he uses those פסוקים for other lessons.

phrases.aramaic: וּלְאַבָּיֵי, אִי לָאו דְּאָמַר רַחֲמָנָא ״הָשֵׁב תָּשִׁיב״,
phrases.english: And according to Abaye, if the Merciful One had not said 'You shall surely return,'
I would have said: he did a forbidden act,

phrases.aramaic: אִי בָּעֵי נַיהְדַּר וְאִי בָּעֵי לָא נַהְדַּר,
phrases.english: if he wants he may return it, and if he wants he need not return it,
so the verse teaches us that he must return it.
(Another version is missing here.)

steps.triggerLanguage: וּלְאַבָּיֵי, אִי לָאו דְּאָמַר רַחֲמָנָא ״הָשֵׁב תָּשִׁיב״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Like step 5, it explains how אביי reads the פסוק that רבא just used.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reassigning a פסוק to a different lesson
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since the forbidden taking takes effect, the lender might keep or return the collateral as he wishes.
steps.terutzMaskana: ״השב תשיב״ requires the lender to return the items the borrower needs.

steps.title: פאה must still be given even after the field is harvested
steps.stepSummary: The תורה forbids harvesting the corner of the field, yet a ברייתא says the owner must still give פאה at every later stage, even from dough. This looks like a refutation of אביי.
steps.simpleTranslation: But what about פאה? The תורה says: "Do not finish off the corner of your field when you harvest." And we learned: the best way to do the מצוה of פאה is to set it aside from grain still standing in the field. If he did not, he sets it aside from the sheaves. If he did not do that either, he sets it aside from the grain pile, as long as he has not yet smoothed the pile. Once he has smoothed it, he first takes off the tithes and then gives the poor their share. In the name of רבי ישמעאל they said: he even sets it aside from the dough. This is a refutation of אביי!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges אביי with the law of פאה. The owner did the forbidden act of harvesting the corner, but the corner still belongs to the poor.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי says a forbidden act still takes effect. If so, once the owner wrongly harvested the corner, it should become fully his. But the ברייתא says he must still give פאה from the sheaves, the pile, and even the dough. That shows the forbidden harvest did not take effect.

keyTerms.meaning: The corner of the field that must be left for the poor
Grain still standing in the field, not yet cut
Sheaves, bundles of cut grain
A pile of threshed grain
He smoothed the pile, the final step that makes the grain obligated in tithes
Dough

steps.confusionAlert: The question is not whether the owner sinned. He clearly did. The question is whether his forbidden harvesting made the corner his. The ברייתא shows it did not.

phrases.english: But there is פאה,
about which the Merciful One said:
"Do not finish off the corner of your field when you harvest,"
and we learned: the mitzva of פאה
is to set it aside from the standing grain;
if he did not set it aside from the standing grain,
he sets it aside from the sheaves;
if he did not set it aside from the sheaves,
he sets it aside from the grain pile,
as long as he has not smoothed it.
If he smoothed it, he tithes it and then gives to him (the poor person);
In the name of רבי ישמעאל they said:
he even sets it aside from the dough.
This is a refutation of אביי!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a new case against אביי's view, after the cases of robbery and collateral were answered.
steps.kashyaTarget: אביי's rule that a forbidden act still takes effect
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The owner harvested the corner against the תורה's command, yet he must still give it to the poor at every stage. So the forbidden harvest did not make it his, against אביי.

steps.title: אביי: an extra word makes פאה a special case
steps.stepSummary: אביי answers that פאה is different, because the תורה says ״תעזוב״ an extra time. That extra word teaches that פאה must still be given even after harvest.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי can tell you: it is different there, because the verse says "you shall leave," and "you shall leave" again, an extra time.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי defends his view by saying פאה has its own special פסוק. His general rule is untouched.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally, for אביי, a forbidden act takes effect. But the תורה repeats ״תעזוב״, and that extra word teaches that with פאה the owner must leave it for the poor no matter what. So פאה is an exception, not a disproof of his rule.

keyTerms.meaning: You shall leave (for the poor)
Extra, an extra word

phrases.english: אביי can say to you:
It is different there,
because the verse says "you shall leave,"
and "you shall leave" is said an extra time.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 9 on behalf of אביי.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Special source makes this case an exception
steps.terutzHavaAmina: פאה proves that forbidden acts do not take effect, against אביי.
steps.terutzMaskana: פאה is a special case because of the extra ״תעזוב״. Elsewhere, forbidden acts still take effect.

steps.title: רבא uses the extra word for someone who makes his vineyard ownerless
steps.stepSummary: רבא does not need the extra ״תעזוב״ for פאה, since for him a forbidden act never takes effect. He uses it to teach a law about someone who makes his vineyard ownerless.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבא can tell you: there is another kind of "leaving" like this one. Which is it? Someone who makes his vineyard ownerless.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains how רבא reads the extra ״תעזוב״. Without this, the extra word would seem to have no job for him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבא, the forbidden harvest does not work anyway, so the פאה law needs no special source. He uses the extra ״תעזוב״ to link another kind of "leaving" to פאה: the case of one who makes his vineyard ownerless. This follows the same pattern as steps 5 and 8, where one side uses the extra פסוק for a different law.

keyTerms.meaning: Leaving, giving something up
One who declares his property ownerless (הפקר)
His vineyard

steps.whatToRemember: The pattern repeats, but the roles switch. In robbery and collateral, רבא (forbidden acts do not take effect) explains each case that looks different with a special פסוק (״אשר גזל״, ״השב תשיב״), and אביי uses those פסוקים for other lessons. In פאה it is reversed: אביי (forbidden acts take effect) explains the exception with the extra ״תעזוב״, and רבא uses that word for the ownerless vineyard.

phrases.english: And רבא can say to you:
There is another kind of "leaving" like this one,
and which is it? It is one who makes his vineyard ownerless.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows how רבא uses the extra word that אביי needed for פאה.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reassigns the extra פסוק to a different law
steps.terutzHavaAmina: If רבא does not need the extra ״תעזוב״ for פאה, the word seems to have no purpose for him.
steps.terutzMaskana: For רבא, the extra ״תעזוב״ teaches about one who makes his vineyard ownerless.

steps.title: The ברייתא about a man who makes his vineyard ownerless
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the ברייתא that רבא learns from the extra ״תעזוב״. If someone makes his vineyard ownerless and then harvests it early in the morning, he must still give the gifts to the poor, but he is exempt from מעשר.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is taught in a ברייתא: If someone makes his vineyard ownerless, then gets up early in the morning and harvests it, he must still leave פרט, עוללות, שכחה and פאה for the poor. But he does not have to separate מעשר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is quoting the source for the law mentioned in the last step, the law רבא learns from the extra ״תעזוב״.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally ownerless produce is free from both the gifts to the poor and from מעשר. Here the owner made the vineyard ownerless and then grabbed it back early in the morning. The extra ״תעזוב״ teaches that he still owes the poor their gifts, but the ברייתא keeps him exempt from מעשר.

keyTerms.meaning: One who makes his property ownerless (הפקר)
Single grapes that fall during the harvest, left for the poor
Small, poorly formed grape clusters, left for the poor
Clusters forgotten during the harvest, left for the poor
Tithe, the tenth part of the produce that must be separated

steps.whatToRemember: For רבא, the extra ״תעזוב״ is not needed for פאה. It teaches that the gifts to the poor still apply to a vineyard that was made ownerless and then harvested by its former owner.

phrases.english: As it is taught in a ברייתא: One who makes his vineyard ownerless,
and got up early in the morning and harvested it,
is obligated in fallen grapes and small clusters,
in forgotten clusters and in פאה,
and is exempt from tithe.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the ברייתא that step 11 said רבא learns from the extra ״תעזוב״.
steps.raayaObject: רבא's use of the extra ״תעזוב״ for a vineyard that was made ownerless
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא ruling that such a vineyard still owes the gifts to the poor but not מעשר

steps.title: Where do אביי and רבא actually disagree?
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בריה דרבא asks רב אשי: we have explained every case so that both אביי and רבא agree. So where is their real disagreement?
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא, the son of רבא, said to רב אשי: Now that we have given all these answers, about what do אביי and רבא actually disagree?
steps.whatsHappening: After all the answers, a new question opens: if every case was explained so that אביי and רבא agree, where do they really argue? This sets up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In each earlier challenge, the side under attack explained the case as a special exception (״השב תשיב״, the extra ״תעזוב״). The result is that both sides agree on all those cases. So רב אחא wants to know if any practical case is left where their dispute about a forbidden act makes a difference.

keyTerms.meaning: We answered, we explained (a case) differently
Answers that explain a case as different or special
About what do they disagree?

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אַחָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרָבָא לְרַב אָשֵׁי:
phrases.english: Rav Acha the son of Rava said to Rav Ashi:
And now that we have given all these answers,
about what do Abaye and Rava disagree?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהַשְׁתָּא דְּשַׁנִּינַן כֹּל הָנֵי שִׁינּוּיֵי, דְּאַבָּיֵי וְרָבָא בְּמַאי פְּלִיגִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Steps back from the case-by-case defenses to ask where the dispute still has practical meaning.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A practical case where אביי and רבא still disagree

steps.title: They disagree about fixed interest
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי answers that אביי and רבא disagree about רבית קצוצה, fixed interest. Their dispute matches רבי אלעזר, who says such interest is taken back from the lender by the judges.
steps.simpleTranslation: They disagree about fixed interest, and it follows רבי אלעזר. For רבי אלעזר said: Fixed interest is taken back by the judges.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי gives the practical case: רבית קצוצה. He starts quoting רבי אלעזר's ruling to show how the dispute plays out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Taking רבית קצוצה is a forbidden act. רבי אלעזר says the court forces the lender to give it back, which fits the idea that a forbidden act does not take effect, so the money never truly became his. The גמרא will go on to show how this matches the two sides.

keyTerms.meaning: Fixed interest, agreed on clearly at the time of the loan, forbidden by the תורה
They disagree
Is taken back by the judges, the court forces it to be returned

steps.whyThisMatters: This turns a theoretical argument about whether a forbidden act takes effect into a real money case: can the borrower get his interest back through the court?

phrases.english: They disagree about fixed interest,
phrases.notes: This is interest that was clearly set when the loan was made, the kind the Torah forbids directly.

phrases.english: and it is like Rabbi Elazar,
for Rabbi Elazar said:
Fixed interest is taken back by the judges,

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The real dispute between אביי and רבא is over רבית קצוצה, linked to רבי אלעזר's ruling that the judges take it back.
